purpose: Preserve the proven host-visible curl --config - transition, enforce its versioned envelope at the server, correlate and bound the response, and prevent duplicate side-effecting relays across engine processes without disabling unrelated model tools.
required_checks: selected Python imports flask, flask_socketio, and requests before any suite starts
all 147 tests pass in nine bounded module invocations
real curl parses a prepared stdin receipt under --version without opening a network connection
missing or mismatched compiled admission, capability, and __probe__ envelopes fail before relay
a two-process claim permits exactly one new relay; completed duplicates replay once; conflict, in-progress, and unknown states do not relay again
chunked box responses are streamed and bounded before decoding; oversized mutable responses become unknown and cannot relay again
sh -n passes for both shell entrypoints
Python compilation, both JSON manifests, git diff --check, exact changed-file coverage, and high-confidence repository secret-pattern scan pass
review_questions: Does prepare perform no network access and leave curl --config - visibly top-level at the host boundary?
Does each prepare generate a fresh request ID and bind version, mode, operation, ID, exact body bytes, and normalized credential bytes?
Do admission and capability routes reject absent, malformed, or mismatched envelopes before any box relay, including designed __probe__?
Does verify require the returned request ID to equal the prepared ID?
Can a side-effecting request ID be relayed more than once after completion, conflict, concurrency, timeout, or an unknown result?
Are transition receipts private, persistent, count bounded, response-size bounded, and expired after the capability lifetime cannot remain valid?
Does operator-root recovery remain compatible while model boots receive no diagnostic, hosting, repository, mailbox, or deployment root?
Does any current model-facing helper still construct an alternate HTTP request or hold a capability directly?
Does the protocol remain independent of model and hosting provider while all unrelated tools remain available?
Does the B1 verifier refuse an unsuitable runtime before launching tests?
Do the corpus, code, tests, and exact manifest describe the same candidate behavior and the same one remaining live readback?
live_resume_after_clean_review: land the exact reviewed overlay without changing a byte
deploy MAIN and FARM at the resulting reviewed commit and prove source identity
resume the existing B1 install manifest at the sole remaining shepherd_alert.py pre-restart readback
continue the existing box restart, health, active-service, Control boot, Worker boot, denial, expiry, revocation, and laptop-retirement proofs
prove an uncompiled valid-capability request receives HTTP 428 and does not reach the box
